headline: Dry and cool through Sunday afternoon around Glendale and Los Angeles, with light rain Sunday night into Monday and a smaller chance midweek before a dry, mild Thanksgiving, while likely record-breaking tides threaten coastal flooding all week.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A weak disturbance passing this afternoon and evening brings only scattered light showers north of Point Conception, a few hundredths of an inch at most, while Glendale and the rest of Los Angeles County stay dry. Highs run around 5 degrees below normal. Tonight, weak northeast winds blow from the land in the usual wind-prone areas but stay below advisory levels, and it turns chilly, with some areas dropping below freezing.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Saturday is dry, and the light winds from the land warm things a bit west of the mountains, with highs in the mid to upper 60s. Dry weather lasts through at least Sunday afternoon, then a weak system brings a decent chance of measurable rain Sunday night into Monday morning, totaling a quarter inch or less with no flooding issues expected. Highs change only slightly from day to day Sunday and Monday.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: The next system, Tuesday night through Wednesday night, doesn't look very impressive. Rain is likely in San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara Counties with 0.10 to 0.50 inch (more around Rocky Butte), while Los Angeles and Ventura Counties have lower chances and a tenth of an inch or less. Thanksgiving Day and Friday look dry as high pressure builds and weak winds from the land develop, with highs in the mid 60s to mid 70s.

coast: Elevated to high surf brings dangerous rip currents and beach conditions Friday, with a High Surf Advisory and a Beach Hazards Statement in effect until 3 PM; strong rip currents remain likely on most west-facing beaches, and surf gradually drops to fairly small at most beaches by Saturday. Extremely high, likely record-breaking tides peak Tuesday through Thanksgiving Day, and new large westerly swells are increasingly likely, with a good chance of high surf on west-facing beaches; together they will likely cause at least moderate, widespread coastal flooding on all coasts, and significant flooding is possible Wednesday and Thursday if a large swell lines up with the highest tides. Coastal Flood Advisories begin at 3 AM Monday (running to 3 AM Wednesday for some beaches and 3 PM Thursday for others), with a Coastal Flood Watch from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon. Offshore, conditions are much improved but remain hazardous for small craft, with Small Craft Advisories ending at 9 PM Friday or 3 AM Saturday depending on the area, then fairly mild Saturday; a weak front Sunday into Monday should have little impact, while a stronger cold front Tuesday night into Wednesday brings the best chance of wind and rain off the Central Coast, possible small-craft-level northwest to west winds south of Point Conception Wednesday and Wednesday night, and large seas returning mid to late week.
watch_for: Below-freezing early mornings in some areas tonight and this weekend.
Light rain Sunday night into Monday morning (a quarter inch or less), and how much reaches Los Angeles County with Wednesday's system.
Likely record tides Tuesday through Thanksgiving plus incoming large swells, with significant coastal flooding possible Wednesday and Thursday.
confidence: Forecasters say the models agree well for both the weekend and next week, giving good confidence in the light rain amounts and a dry Thanksgiving; the biggest uncertainty is whether a large swell coincides with the extreme tides.
